claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To assess this properly, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under 16, or any older children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I do. I have one child - Alex, who is 17 and lives with me at home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Since Alex is 17 and lives with you, I need to ask:

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (for example, school, college, university, or an approved apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in any education or training at the moment. They finished school but haven't started anything else yet.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Since Alex is 17 and no longer in approved education or training, I need to ask:

**Has Alex registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services since leaving education?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't registered with a careers service or the armed forces.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Based on the information you've provided, let me explain the situation:

According to Child Benefit rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and live in the UK. For children aged 16 or over, you can usually continue to receive Child Benefit if they stay in approved education or training.

However, there is a provision that allows you to apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services.

In Alex's case, since they are 17, have left education, and have not registered with a careers service or the armed forces, you would unfortunately not be eligible to continue receiving Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

However, there is a positive note: if Alex were to register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, you would be able to apply for Child Benefit to continue for a further 20 weeks from the date of that registration. This could be worth exploring if Alex is considering their next steps.

Is there anything else I can help you with regarding this matter?
